our proposed method is the first method that is able to achieve state of the art performance on the MSR Action3D dataset and the NTU RGB+ D dataset, while requiring much less computation for training, and is also able to perform well on the challenging NTU RGB+DW dataset.

the proposed representation and the ResNet based D CNN architecture are able to learn discriminative features from 3D motion sequences, which are then used for effective classification of human actions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we introduce a new representation for 3d action recognition, and a new learning model to learn the 3D action representations.
the proposed representation and the trained D CNNs provide a very powerful tool for learning and recognizing 3D human actions from skeleton sequences.

the color encoding based skeleton representation can be used as a general purpose 3D motion feature representation, and D CNNs can be trained on the representation to recognize human actions in videos.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D motion information can be efficiently represented as RGB images and learned by D CNNs.
a simple color encoding process can transform skeleton sequences into a compact representation that can be easily learned by a powerful D CNN architecture.
the ResNet architecture is able to effectively learn 3D human motion representations from the proposed skeleton based image representations.
